Macquarie Island (port locode AUMQI), aka Macca, is located halfway between Tasmania and Antarctica (Anderson Peninsula) and Antarctica-New Zealand (approx 630 km / 390 mi southwest of Auckland Island NZ).

Since 1900, this territory has belonged to Australia's Tasmania state. In 1978, it was designated "Tasmanian State Reserve" and since 1997 is listed as a "UNESCO World Heritage Site". The island has length 34 km (21 mi), width 5 km (3 mi), total area approx 128 km2 (49 mi2) and highest elevation point (Mt Hamilton) is 410 m (1345 ft).

The island is best known for its large colony of royal penguins and the Macquarie Island Station, a research station permanently maintained by the Australian Antarctic Division since 1947. Base's personnel is the island's only population (20-40 people through the year). Near the station, there is a heliport serving aircraft deployed from icebreaking ships and other supply vessels.

The newest Australian icebreaker RSV Nuyina (launched 2019) supplies with cargo, equipment and personnel four permanent Australian bases - three in Antarctica (Mawson, Davis, Casey) and one on Macquarie Island. Additionally, the ship serves as a research laboratory with passenger capacity up to 116 scientific staff.

As a cruise port, Macquarie Island is included (as an overnight stay) in the itinerary program of Ponant's newest superyacht - Le Laperouse (2018-built).

Cruise ships often anchor at Sandy Bay (on the island's east coast) for wildlife viewing: royal and king penguins and southern elephant seals.
